subsystems.name: Structural frame
subsystems.role: rigid skeleton that holds the motherboard, power supply and expansion cards in alignment.

subsystems.name: Exterior panels
subsystems.role: protect components from dust, impact and electromagnetic interference while shaping the look.

subsystems.name: Airflow and cooling mounts
subsystems.role: guide cool air across hot components and exhaust warm air.

subsystems.name: Drive and power mounting
subsystems.role: secures storage devices and the power supply.

subsystems.name: Front I/O and cable management
subsystems.role: gives the user external connections and keeps internal wiring tidy.

subsystems.name: Expansion and tool-less mechanisms
subsystems.role: allow quick installation and removal of cards, drives and panels.

buildSteps.title: Design and prototype
buildSteps.detail: Engineers model the case in CAD, check it against standard motherboard and power-supply dimensions, and simulate airflow to place vents and fan mounts.

buildSteps.title: Cut and stamp sheet metal
buildSteps.detail: Coils of steel or aluminium are fed through presses that punch holes for fans, cables and screws, then bend the flat sheet into trays and panels.

buildSteps.title: Join the frame
buildSteps.detail: Spot welding, riveting or screws lock the motherboard tray, power-supply cage and drive mounts into a rigid box.

buildSteps.title: Finish the surfaces
buildSteps.detail: Metal parts are cleaned and powder-coated or anodised for corrosion resistance and colour.

buildSteps.title: Make panels and bezels
buildSteps.detail: Tempered glass is cut, edge-ground and sometimes tinted; plastic front bezels and mesh filters are injection-moulded or stamped.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and wire
buildSteps.detail: Standoffs, drive cages, fan mounts, front-panel connectors and cable-routing grommets are fitted by hand or on a short assembly line.

buildSteps.title: Test and pack
buildSteps.detail: A sample is checked for fit, airflow and electrical continuity, then the case is packed with screws, standoffs and manuals.

prerequisites.tech: Standard form factors (ATX, Micro-ATX, Mini-ITX, SFX)
prerequisites.why: without agreed dimensions, motherboards and power supplies would not fit any case.
the frame and panels are mass-produced from flat steel or aluminium.
front bezels, fan mounts and cable grommets are moulded to complex shapes.
glass side panels must be strong and shatter into small, safe pieces if broken.
cases and coolers rely on common hole spacings for 120 mm and 140 mm fans.

pathway.milestone: mesh-front, glass-side cases with USB-C front ports and tool-less drive trays
pathway.unlocks: easy building and better airflow for high-power components.

pathway.milestone: cases designed around larger fans (180 mm and above) and quieter bearings
pathway.unlocks: more airflow at lower noise levels.

pathway.milestone: modular, reconfigurable interiors that accept many form factors and layouts
pathway.unlocks: one case can be reused across multiple builds and upgrades.

pathway.milestone: cases with integrated cooling, sensing and power delivery
pathway.unlocks: less internal cabling and simpler assembly for non-specialists.
